reason: The clock is not the problem. The idea's own pre-registered gate is. If the gate passes, the path is short: about 20 min of CPU fits, a dataset upload, one exp56 kernel change, a 40 min T4 dummy run after the 26 Sep 00:00 UTC reset, and 7-10 h of scoring. That gives a score around 26 Sep 08:00-17:00 UTC with about 2.5 days of slack. But the rule says 'Fail -> stop; no probe', and as written the gate very likely fails whatever the head quality. (1) Mean-shift criterion (all-peak shift within 0.2 um of REF on every axis). REF is non-debiased and trained on one embryo, so it learns that embryo's annotation offset. In the same fold, P (non-debiased, trained on 6bba) had all-peak mean shift z +0.567 um, while debiased Q had -0.123 (out_full_P/Q report.json, kill_test.sample_mean_shift_new_zyx). The expected gap is about 0.5-0.7 um, more than 0.2 um. Debias removes exactly that offset by design, so the criterion contradicts the mechanism. Even against the public head, Q's gap is 0.212 um, which is WARN territory. (2) Distance criterion, direction 44b6->6bba. Q = 1.5875 um is worse than the non-debiased P = 1.5699 (the 44b6 offset partly transfers to 6bba). Candidate <= 0.97 x REF therefore needs REF >= 1.637, meaning the 10-stem REF must be at least 4.3 % worse than the 71-video P from data volume alone: about a coin flip. The 6bba->44b6 direction likely passes (Q/P = 0.949). (3) 7 um re-match >= 'none': Q's margins are only +4 (20116 vs 20112) and +2 (112256 vs 112254), so bag/seed noise can flip them. (4) Per-video win rate vs none passes easily (Q 68/71 = 0.96, 109/128 = 0.85). (5) --balance embryo does nothing in the single-embryo held-out folds, so the gate never tests the balancing it is meant to justify. P(gate as written passes) is about 0.05-0.10; with the shift criterion repaired it is about 0.35-0.45. So P(scored probe by 29 Sep 10:00) is about 0.05-0.4, below 0.70. The number checks mostly hold: Q -8.1 % / -7.7 % vs none, fits 26-35 s, 125,700 pairs of which 106,452 are 6bba, and none-bias z +0.177 / +0.824. Two notes: the 'x138 validator stems' are the script's reconstruction (x138_probable_train), not a known list; and in-embryo Q is still worse than the public head (+6.3 % / +1.3 %). Even when scored, expected +0.0005 against 0.003 LB noise means the probe cannot resolve its own question.
fix_if_any: Fix the gate before running anything, then run it today (it is about 20 min of CPU). (a) Drop the REF-shift criterion or make it one-sided. Require the candidate's all-peak mean shift to be within 0.25 um of the PUBLIC head on every axis, and its |mean shift| to be no larger than REF's. That checks for convention learning without penalising debias. (b) Keep 'mean distance <= 0.97 x REF in both directions' and add 'no worse than P-analog (non-debiased, all videos of the training embryo) by more than 1 %'. (c) Change m7 to '>= none - 20', because counts within +-5 of 20k/112k are noise. (d) Test --balance separately: it can only be judged on leak5 folds (both embryos in train) through the per-embryo breakdown. Say so in the gate, and do not claim the embryo-held-out gate validates it. Then use the fixed critical path below. Present it as a private-robustness candidate for F2, not a public probe: the public LB cannot resolve +0.0005, so a scored probe is only a crash/no-harm check (nodes within +-1 % of exp56, score >= #34 - 0.003).
realistic_public_gain: -0.002..+0.002, central about +0.0005. This matches the idea's own arithmetic: 0.004 localisation value x 0-40 % further relative distance cut, minus the convention risk. That is below the 0.003 LB noise, so it is not measurable with one probe.
realistic_private_gain: 0..+0.002 (guess). It depends on how far 199-video debiased training generalises to unseen embryos. The gate evidence against a fair out-of-embryo reference has not been computed yet.
critical_path: Machines and owners: this container (no data, no Kaggle) can only write code. The captures are Kaggle kernel outputs vitaliineibauer/biohub-chcap-{44b6-s0of2,s1of2,6bba-s0..3of4,pilot}, downloaded to experiments/coordhead_retrain/captures on the Windows machine that ran P/Q. The trainer also needs the train geffs through --data-dir. So Vitalii's Claude session plus his machine does the fits; friend A is not needed. 25 Sep 11:30-14:00: agent adds --balance/--ref-stems/--bag/--distill-public to tools/train_coordhead.py, with a synthetic-capture unit test, and the main session commits it. 14:00-14:45: Vitalii's machine runs, under the fixed gate, REF x2 (about 5 s each), none, a P-analog, a 5-seed bag x2 folds (about 5 min), and leak5 folds for --balance (about 3 min). Total CPU is about 15 min, plus about 5 min to load the 199 captures. 14:45: gate decision, logged in report.json; if it fails, stop. 15:00-15:30: 199-video balanced bag plus distillation (about 5 min), sha256, then kaggle datasets create vitaliineibauer/biohub-coordhead-v2 (processing 5-15 min). 15:30-16:30: exp58 = exp56 with dataset_sources changed from anvithpothula/biohub-v1284-head-s075 to the v2 dataset and the rglob at cell 4 line 511 retargeted. It must match exactly one file (the kernel raises 'mount mismatch' otherwise), and the kernel must print the new sha. Build via tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138. 17:00-20:00: #34 scores; exp58 is an A/B against #34 whatever the result. 26 Sep 00:00 UTC: vitaliineibauer GPU quota resets (0 GPU-h before, so no dummy run on 25 Sep). 00:05-00:50: private T4 dummy run, about 30-40 min (exp51 took 1,713 s). Check node count vs exp56 within +-1 % and the head sha. Submit about 01:00 if the user has pre-approved (there is precedent from the 24 Sep 21:05 pre-approval); otherwise at about 07:00 UTC when the user wakes. Scoring: the x138 runtime guard is at 27,000 s, so 7-10 h, giving a score at about 08:00-11:00 or 14:00-17:00 on 26 Sep. Slack to 29 Sep 10:00 is about 65 h, so even a failed dummy run can be retried on 26-27 Sep. Conflicts are minor: 20 slots from 26-29 Sep, 30 GPU-h/week at about 0.7 h per dummy run. Uncertain (guess): whether hidden-test scoring reruns count toward the GPU quota. Overall P(score before the deadline) = P(gate passes) x about 0.9, which is about 0.05-0.09 with the gate as written and about 0.3-0.4 with the gate fixed as proposed.
